assigned.title: Contract module boundaries
assigned.acceptance: Shared vocabularies live in their own leaf modules, domain contracts live in one module each, index.ts is a re-export-only compatibility barrel rather than the authoritative public surface, and a wildcard exports map lets a new domain contract be added without touching package metadata or the barrel; no cycle-driven z.lazy remains and structural regressions prove the boundary rather than merely reflecting it; no schema behaviour changes

repo-validate.evidence: npm run repo:validate, exit 0, and node scripts/ai-control-plane.mjs validate 0 at 66 tasks. NO CODE WAS WRITTEN FOR PL-AI-0006 THIS ROUND: the acceptance is already satisfied at HEAD and this round performed the provenance repair -- a narrowing of allowedPaths from four wildcards to the exact 51 files f06dec1 wrote, then reconciliation to 18ce472. repo:validate is on this task's gate list rather than typecheck because the deliverable is a module boundary and the repository validator is what checks the shape of the tree. Also run and green at this head: turbo typecheck 0 (21/21), lint 0 (11/11), build 0 (11/11).

unit.evidence: npx turbo run test --force, exit 0, 20 of 20, 2734 passed 1 skipped. THE SUITE THAT IS THIS TASK'S ACCEPTANCE IS packages/contracts/src/module-boundary.test.ts, run in isolation for this gate: 15 tests, all passing. It asserts the four properties the acceptance names, mechanically rather than by convention -- index.ts contains nothing but re-export statements and imports no zod, no package-internal module reaches the barrel, no shared/** module imports from domains/**, and every exported domain and shared subpath resolves to a real file. It also carries the z.lazy guard the split earned: z.lazy may only defer a schema declared in the SAME file, because using it to reach a symbol elsewhere means an initialisation cycle is being worked around rather than removed. That file exists BECAUSE the previous layout also 'currently happened to' work, which is the strongest evidence the boundary is enforced rather than described. The unreproducible media-inspection failure recorded on PL-0503's unit gate at this same tree applies to this run too and is not repeated here; see that gate for the full statement.

assigned.notes: EVIDENCE-BASED NARROWING 2026-09-22, under the procedure gpt-architect ratified as general at b0344606887e4b91e1d832b7c082bb95059d151b. allowedPaths were ["packages/contracts/**","packages/media-engine/**","packages/provider-sdk/**","apps/web/**"] and are now the EXACT 51 files commit f06dec1 wrote -- 'PL-AI-0006: split contracts into shared vocabularies and domain modules'. That commit names this task alone in its subject, so the whole of it is attributed without judgement calls; the only other commit mentioning the id, 6845e37, DEFINES the task and writes no implementation. THIS SURFACE IS LARGE AND THAT IS THE CORRECT ANSWER RATHER THAN A FAILURE TO NARROW. Splitting a contracts barrel rewrites every import site, so 33 of the 51 files are consumers in apps/web, media-engine and provider-sdk whose imports the split changed. The ruling is explicit that a file genuinely written to stays, and dropping the consumers would have produced a tidier declaration that lied about what the task did. The enforced surface is nonetheless disjoint from every other active task, verified rather than assumed: none of the 51 is a telemetry, observability, progress, watchlist or writer-epoch file, so PL-0403, PL-0404 and PL-0503 are untouched by it. THE ACCEPTANCE IS ALREADY SATISFIED AT HEAD and was checked before any of this: packages/contracts/src has shared/ leaf vocabularies and domains/ modules, index.ts is twelve export-star lines, and module-boundary.test.ts enforces the four properties mechanically. This task needs reconciliation and review, not implementation.
